items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: Eddie Fife was in Larchmont and up in Greenwich Connecticut there was a piano player, Dick Wellstood, and the bass player, Charlie Traeger. And out of this group we gradually had jam sessions to get together. We got a group together that, we called ourselves The Wildcats.

ctx.x: That’s a great story. Now you managed to get your own group together in high school, The Wildcats.

Yeah. I was playing with these older fellas and then I gradually found out about other musicians around the county. Eddie Fife was in Larchmont and up in Greenwich Connecticut there was a piano player, Dick Wellstood, and the bass player, Charlie Traeger. And out of this group we gradually had jam sessions to get together. We got a group together that, we called ourselves The Wildcats. And we started playing around. And we all went down to Jimmy Ryan’s for one of their Sunday sessions. And we got friendly with…
There was a comment in one of the jazz books that said that the first American revival group of consequence in the East, talking about The Wildcats.

items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: But the players that were my contemporaries that are still active are Dick Wellstead on piano, who was from Greenwich, Connecticut, and Johnny Glazel, who played trumpet from Scarsdale, and Charlie Traeger was a bass player from Greenwich.

ctx.x: That group has been written up, I know at times, in the old magazines and all and other wives. Can you tell some of the other fellows that you played with when you started?

Yeah. Well, there was an earlier group that were older than I who have not kept up their professional activities. But the players that were my contemporaries that are still active are Dick Wellstead on piano, who was from Greenwich, Connecticut, and Johnny Glazel, who played trumpet from Scarsdale, and Charlie Traeger was a bass player from Greenwich. He's still playing. Let me see. Jerry Blumberg came in on the scene later. He was from Baltimore.
Jerry was here two weeks ago. He didn't see him.
